title: php2shell: pre-auth RCE in the PHP engine (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
summary: Two pre-auth remote code execution bugs in PHP itself (CVSSv4 9.2 each) hit PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed before any app code runs; exploitation is reported by Amazon, Cloudflare and watchTowr (CISA's early advisory said none was observed at publication), and 7.4-8.1 have no official fixed release.
notes: CVE-2026-109618: out-of-memory corruption of partially initialized request data. CVE-2026-109619: use-after-free from stale global state across requests on the same worker (memory disclosure confirmed). mod_php is highest risk. Calif reports pre-auth RCE on WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. First exploitation attempts seen 2026-10-17. Distro/LTS vendors got patches early and may backport without changing the upstream version string, so check the vendor advisory before trusting a version-only verdict.

ranges.note: 5.4-7.3 EOL, no fix; 7.4-8.1 no official release (minimal source backports only) - check your distro/LTS vendor

preconditions.mitigation: memory_limit=-1 set so applications cannot override it (php_admin_value / php_admin_flag)

remediation.step: Confirm the PHP version and SAPI that actually serves requests
remediation.why: Exposure depends on the web-serving PHP (FPM/mod_php/cgi), not the CLI on your laptop.

any: docker compose exec <service> php -i | grep -Ei 'Server API|upload_progress.enabled|memory_limit'

remediation.step: Isolate or shield internet-facing PHP apps until patched
remediation.why: Exploitation is under way and bugs fire before app code; CERT-EU advises isolating exposed apps.
remediation.danger: WAF rules (e.g. Cloudflare's) are a stopgap, not a fix.

any: Put the site behind maintenance mode / IP allowlist, or enable your WAF's php2shell rules

remediation.step: Apply interim ini mitigations and restart ALL PHP workers
remediation.why: Blocks the known triggers while you schedule the upgrade.
remediation.danger: Settings only take effect after every worker restarts; container/cgroup memory limits are NOT a mitigation; these settings do not make PHP safe.

linux: sudo systemctl restart php8.3-fpm   # match your version

remediation.step: Upgrade PHP to a fixed release
remediation.why: The only complete fix: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35; older branches need a vendor build or a branch upgrade.

any: Bump the FROM tag (e.g. php:8.3.36-fpm) then: docker compose build --pull && docker compose up -d
linux: sudo apt-get update && apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -i php
Check your distro security tracker: backported fixes may keep the old version string
windows: Download the fixed build from https://windows.php.net/download/

remediation.step: Verify the fix where the code runs
remediation.why: Proves the running workers, not just the image or package, are patched.

remediation.step: Hunt for signs of exploitation since 2026-10-17
remediation.why: Exploitation began before disclosure; a patched server can still carry a webshell.
remediation.danger: If you find a webshell or unknown admin user, treat the host as compromised: contain first, then rotate DB and app secrets (wp-config.php, .env) from a clean machine.

any: Review CMS admin users created since 2026-10-17

remediation.why: 5.4-7.3 will never get a fix; 7.4-8.1 have no official release.

any: Plan an upgrade to a supported branch (8.2+) or a vendor LTS with a published php2shell patch
